steps: Unpack & check contents
Lay all parts on a clean, soft, dry surface and check them against the parts list. Use extreme caution handling the glass.

Package contents: electric fireplace, instruction manual, remote control and batteries, wall mounting bracket, smoked crushed glass (boxed), glass suction clamp, mounting screw packet, power cord.

Tools (not included): Phillips screwdriver, stud finder, level, tape measure, electric drill, 1/4" wood drill bit.

Keep plastic packaging and small parts away from young children.
Choose the installation option
Wall mounted on the supplied bracket, or recessed: single-sided (both side block-off plates stay on), corner (remove one) or 3-sided bay (remove both). Pick a dry spot away from drapes and furniture.

Follow all national and local building and electrical codes. Don't store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids near the heater. Using the supplied power cord, plan where it reaches an electrical box; a recessed installation must be hardwired by a licensed electrician (NFPA 70).

Meets H.U.D. construction and safety standards for manufactured homes when installed per the manual.
Set up the side cover plates

Standard: discard the "C" finishing trim and refit both cover plates. Corner: on the open side discard the cover plate and refit the trim; on the closed side discard the trim. 3-sided: discard both cover plates and refit the "C" trim.

The screws holding each side cover plate also hold the finishing trim.

  • Standard: remove the screws, discard the "C"-shaped trim, refit the cover plate and screws on both sides. Framing then sits flush with the body and finishing material butts the 1/2" finishing edge.
  • Corner: on the side with exposed glass, discard the cover plate and reinstall the finishing trim (finishing material butts against it). On the other side, discard the trim and refit the cover plate.
  • 3-sided (bay): on each side, discard the cover plate and reinstall the "C" trim with the same screws.
Frame the rough opening
Frame to the A / B / C opening for your installation type (Figures 2.1–2.3). Clearances to the unit are 0"; keep combustibles 36" (914mm) from the front.
Fasten the nailing flanges
Fold out the flanges that come attached (2 on top, 2 along the bottom) and secure the unit to the framing.
Electrical connection

Recessed installs must be hardwired by a licensed electrician (NFPA 70). Remove the (4) electrical box cover screws, move the cable clamp to the side, top or rear via the knock-out plate, connect and refit the cover.

Ships ready for hardwiring or the supplied power cord; the cable clamp secures either. Wall mounted with the optional Floating Mantel Kit, put the cable clamp on the side.

Rating120VAC, 60Hz, 1500W
CircuitDedicated 15 Amp (or higher) breaker
Mantel, facing & trim

Keep the combined wall bump-out, finishing material and combustible mantel within a 12" (305mm) projection; finishing material up to 1/2" (13mm) butts the finishing edges. Optional surround or trim: single-sided installs only.

A combustible wall projection of up to 12" (305mm) is allowed starting at the top finishing edge; mantel projections must fall within it. No material may extend inside the finishing edges or block the viewing glass. Material thicker than 1/2" (13mm) leaves part of its edge exposed.

Rectangle surround (optional)

For an unfinished or exposed edge of drywall, tile or wood. Remove the (2) Phillips screws above the viewing glass; fit the base bracket with its tab inside the air intake louver (the only item allowed inside the intake openings; position per Figures 2.7–2.9); fit the adjustable magnetic hanging brackets; hang the surround with its larger (deeper) flange at the bottom, since at the top it may cover the heater vents; hold the bottom with the supplied magnets.

4-piece finishing trim (optional)

For a smooth wall finish or very thin finishing materials. Top and bottom pieces first, then the sides, with the supplied double sided adhesive tape.
Wall mount (instead of recessed)
Remove the (2) bracket screws, fasten the bracket to studs with all the supplied screws (holes 16" apart; no drywall anchors), hang the unit and refit the (2) screws.

If the bracket holes don't line up with studs, add wood structure. Check outlet reach, finishing material, hearth, mantel and any TV or artwork before choosing the spot.

Floating Mantel Kit (optional; e50 and e64 only)

  1. Remove the 3 screws on each side and fit the kit's brackets (right and left side specific).
  2. Wall-mount the unit as above.
  3. Slide the bottom section onto the brackets until it rests against the wall, its top under the bottom finishing edge; don't chip it.
  4. Attach the two mantel legs with (8) screws, (4) per side.
  5. Slide the top assembly down so the legs drop into the bottom section's pockets.
  6. Pushing down on the top, drive screws through the bracket holes on the underside, (3) per side.

Optional: toenail extra screws (not supplied; predrill) through the underside of the top section into the wall. Keep the electrical box faceplate within the shaded area of Figure 2.17 (p. 23); the cord can run along the right mantel leg.
Media & log set

With the unit in its final position, remove any trim and the glass front, spread the supplied crushed media evenly over the full width and depth of the floor, add the optional log set, then refit the glass.

Glass front

  1. Remove any front trim.
  2. With one hand on the glass, remove the screws and brackets at its top right and left; keep them.
  3. Remove the two screws securing the bottom glass trim / retainer.
  4. Lift the glass away and lay it face down on a soft, non-abrasive surface.
  5. Refit: hold the glass, secure the bottom trim / retainer, then the two top clips and screws.

Log sets (optional)

Traditional (OSE-TLS) or birch (OSE-BLS). The (4) charred logs go in front of the pulsating ember bed LEDs, then the remaining logs. Layouts for each model are photos on pp. 35–40; some logs may not be used in the e50 and e64.
Pair the remote & test
Main switch on (standby); hold the two control-panel buttons marked in Figure 5.1 for 5 seconds, release, press power on the remote. Confirm power turns the unit on and off; repeat if not.

panels.title: Remote won't control the unit
items: Idle 60 s → safe mode: press power once to unlock, again to switch on/off
Lock icon shown → hold on/off 60 s to unlock
Control-panel rocker switch off → must be on
Erratic remote → remove batteries to reset to factory settings; refit observing polarity
No on/off after pairing → repeat pairing

panels.title: No heat / wrong cycling
items: Remote at the unit's front or near a window → false temperature, inaccurate on/off
Remote must be in the same room, screen up, sensor uncovered
Main power switch turned off, then fire turned on manually → heat function won't work
Timer at 0 minutes → whole appliance shuts off

panels.title: Malfunction / overheating
items: Any malfunction → disconnect at service panel; authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspection before reuse
Faulty outlet or loose plug → arcing / outlet overheating
Extension cord or power strip → not permitted
Draws more current than other small heaters → may overheat where others didn't
Dust, lint or blockage at vents / intakes → fire risk; keep clear

turnon.title: Turning it on and off
turnon.html:
Your fireplace has two sets of controls: the control panel on the fireplace and the remote.

On the fireplace

  1. Push the main power switch to I. The main power light comes on.
  2. Press the manual switch button to turn the fire on. Press it again to turn it off.
  3. For heat, press the heater button (see Heat and thermostat).

Every button press on the panel beeps. That just means it registered.

From the remote

The rocker switch on the control panel has to be on. Then press power to turn the fireplace on or off. If the remote hasn't been used in the last 60 seconds, press power once to unlock it, then press it again.

First time on: a slight odor is normal. It shouldn't come back unless the fireplace sits unused for a long time.

Fully off

To disconnect the heater, turn the controls off, then turn off the power to its circuit at the main panel.

heat.title: Heat and the thermostat
heat.html:
The heater gives supplemental heat. It isn't meant to be your home's main heat source.

Two heat levels

Press Heater onceHalf power · 750W
Press it againFull power · 1500W

On the control panel, a third press turns the heater off. On the remote, the screen shows an off, half-power or full-power heating icon.

Let the remote hold a temperature

  1. Press the up or down arrow to choose a temperature.
  2. Press SET, or just stop pressing for 3 seconds, to save it.

The heater then turns itself on and off. For example, set to 70°F, it starts on its own when the room is at 66°F. It works to a +/- 3°F tolerance. Hold SET for 6 seconds to switch between °F and °C.

The remote is the thermostat. Keep it in the same room, screen facing up, with its temperature sensor uncovered. Don't leave it in front of the fireplace or by a warm spot like a window, or it will read the wrong temperature.

Without the remote

Set the thermostat above room temperature, then turn the remote off. Everything then works from the control panel. If the main power switch is turned off and you turn the fire on manually again, the heat won't work.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote also works as the fireplace's thermostat, so where you keep it matters (see Heat and thermostat).

Waking it up

After 60 seconds without use, the remote goes into safe mode. Press the "unlock" button before you use it; the screen backlight comes on. To switch the fireplace on or off after the remote has been idle, press power once to unlock it, then press power again.

Saving a setting

Press SET, or stop pressing buttons for 3 seconds, and your setting is saved.

Locking the remote

Hold the on/off button for 60 seconds to lock it. A lock icon appears. Hold it for another 60 seconds to unlock.

Pairing it to the fireplace

  1. Turn on the main switch so the fire is in standby.
  2. Press and hold the two pairing buttons on the fireplace's control panel for 5 seconds. They're marked on the control-panel drawing on p. 41 of the manual.
  3. Release, then press power on the remote.
  4. Test it: power should turn the fireplace on and off. If it doesn't, repeat these steps.

effects.title: Flame, light and sound effects
effects.html:
You can change how the fire looks from the remote or from the control panel on the fireplace.

From the remote

  • Flame: press the flame button and its icon flashes. The up and down arrows set the flame brightness (5 settings, from full flame to no flame). The minus (-) and plus (+) buttons pick a color, 1 to 4.
  • Down light: press the down LED button, then use the up and down arrows for brightness (5 settings, from maximum brightness to no light).
  • Floor LEDs: press the floor LED button. Up and down set the brightness (5 settings); minus and plus pick a color, 1 to 13.
  • Press an effect button a second time to cycle through its colors. Keep pressing until you like what you see.
  • Glowing embers: a red LED pulses in the ember bed. Hold the floor LED button for 5 seconds to turn it on or off.
  • Crackling sound: the background sound button sets the wood-crackling volume: low, medium, high or mute.
Maker's website: Ember Bed 13 colors, 5 intensity levels. In the manual, 13 colors and 5 brightness settings are the floor LEDs; the ember bed is a red LED that pulses (p. 45).

From the control panel

The flame button steps through four flame settings. The down light button cycles seven colors and the floor LED button thirteen. With the fire on, hold either one for 3 seconds until it beeps to start a mode; hold another 3 seconds for the next. Modes are pulse or solid, single color or color changing. Pick your color first if you want a single-color mode.

timer.title: Timer and clock
timer.html:
Shut-off timer

Press the timer button on the remote to step through times from 30 minutes to 8 hours. The timer controls the whole fireplace. When it reaches 0 minutes, the fireplace shuts off.

Setting the remote's clock

  1. Turn the remote on.
  2. Hold the clock button for 5 seconds. The display goes blank except for the time at the bottom.
  3. Press SET. The hour blinks; change it with the up and down arrows.
  4. Press SET again to move to the minutes, and adjust them.
  5. Press SET once more to set the clock.
Each time you replace the remote's batteries, you'll need to set the clock again.

clean.title: Cleaning the fireplace and glass
clean.html:
Always turn the power off first: set the toggle switch on the control panel to off and disconnect the heater from its power supply.

  • Clean the air inlet and heater area regularly. Keep them free of dust and pet hair.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners.
  • Never spray liquid directly onto the fireplace, rinse it, or let it get wet.
  • Glass: spray glass cleaner onto a cloth, wipe the glass, then dry it with a lint-free cloth.
Note: the safety instructions say to unplug it and clean the air vents with a vacuum only (p. 7); the maintenance section says to clean the air inlet and heater area with a cloth or vacuum (p. 46).

If you take the glass out

The glass shatters if it takes a hard knock. Take extra care that its corners don't hit a hard surface.

  • Wear safety gloves and glasses.
  • Lay the glass on a soft surface.
  • Use two people for the 64" and 80" fireplaces.
  • The suction cups only help you tilt the glass back. Don't carry its weight by them.

battery.title: Remote batteries and reset
battery.html:
The remote runs on three AAA batteries.

Remote(3) 1.5V AAA
  • Replace them when the remote's battery indicator shows empty.
  • Use the correct type, 1.5V AAA, and put them in the right way round.
  • Set the remote's clock again after every battery change.

Resetting the remote

If the remote doesn't work correctly, reset it to factory settings: open the back cover, take the batteries out, then put them back in, matching the polarity marks.

The pairing steps are under Use the remote.

safety.title: Safety around the heater
safety.html:
• The heater is hot when it's running. Don't let bare skin touch hot surfaces.
  • Keep furniture, pillows, bedding, papers, clothes and curtains at least 36" (914mm) from the front.
  • Take extreme care when children are near, and when it's left running unattended.
  • Plug it straight into a wall outlet. Never use an extension cord or power strip.
  • Don't use an old or cracked outlet, or one with loose wires. Check that the plug fits tight; a loose plug can overheat the outlet.
  • This heater draws more current than other small heaters, so overheating can happen even where other heaters were fine.
  • Don't block the air intakes or exhaust, and don't let anything get into the openings.
  • It has hot and sparking parts inside. Don't use it where gasoline, paint or flammable liquids are used or stored.
  • Indoors only, and never let it get wet.
If it malfunctions, stop using it. Turn off the power at the service panel and have an authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspect it before you use it again.

It's for supplemental heat only, not a primary heat source.

trouble.title: When something isn't working
trouble.html:
The remote does nothing

  • After 60 seconds idle it's in safe mode. Press power once to unlock it, then again.
  • A lock icon means it's locked. Hold on/off for 60 seconds to unlock.
  • The rocker switch on the fireplace's control panel must be on.
  • Battery indicator empty? Replace the three AAA batteries.
  • Still not right? Take the batteries out to reset it to factory settings.
  • Just paired it and the fireplace won't turn on and off? Repeat the pairing steps.

The heat doesn't come on when you expect

  • The remote is the thermostat. In front of the fireplace or near a window it reads the wrong temperature. Keep it in the same room, screen up, sensor uncovered.
  • The thermostat works to a +/- 3°F tolerance.
  • If the main power switch was turned off and the fire turned back on manually, the heat won't work.
  • When the timer reaches 0 minutes, the whole fireplace shuts off.
After any malfunction, don't keep using it. Turn off the power at the service panel and have an authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspect it.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Note: the warranty page is headed "Limited Lifetime Warranty" (p. 49, also in the contents on p. 5), but its coverage section gives the term as "2 Year Limited Warranty": all parts for 2 years and labor reimbursement for 1 year.

Kozy Heat's maker, Hussong Mfg., covers defects in materials and workmanship for the original purchaser, starting on the date of purchase. In a new home, coverage starts at first occupancy or six months after the dealer's sale, whichever comes first.

Parts2 years
Labor reimbursement1 year, paid to an authorized dealer only
  • Only fireplaces bought through an authorized Kozy Heat dealer or distributor are covered.
  • No documents to send in. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model.
  • It doesn't transfer to a new owner.

Not covered, or voids it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized service technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual.
  • Normal wear: paint, batteries, glass discoloration, and finish color changes.
  • Damp places such as outdoors, porches and laundry rooms, or water damage.
  • Power interruptions or fluctuations, misuse, or unapproved parts or changes.
  • How well it heats your space.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Rating120VAC, 60Hz, 1500W
CircuitDedicated 15 Amp (or higher) breaker
Power cordSupplied; three prongs (two flat blades, one round ground pin)
Recessed installHardwired · licensed electrician · NFPA 70

Ships for either hardwiring or the supplied power cord; recessed installations must be hardwired. Corded: plug directly into a wall receptacle, never an extension cord or relocation power tap. With no 3-slot receptacle an adapter (not included) must be used, its green grounding lug connected to a permanent ground such as a properly grounded outlet box; don't use the adapter where a three-slot grounded receptacle is available.

The cable clamp moves to the side, top or rear via a knock-out plate; side position with the Floating Mantel Kit.

specHeat.title: Heater output
specHeat.html:
Half power750W
Full power1500W
Thermostat tolerance+/- 3°F

Heater button (panel or remote): first press half power, second press full; a third press on the control panel turns the heater off. The thermostat is the remote: same room as the unit, screen up, sensor uncovered, not in front of the unit or near a window. Supplemental heat only.

specMantel.html:

review.notes: Single combined installation and operation manual (Rev. 5, September 2024). It gives no BTU output, weight or viewing-area figure, so catalog electric_btu_max 5000, weight_lb 133/156/212 and view_area can't be checked; 1500W and the 0"/36" clearances match pp. 8 and 12. Appliance (Figure 1.1, p. 9) and framed-opening (Figures 2.1-2.3, pp. 13-15) dimensions are lettered drawings with no legend in the text: the guide repeats the letter values as printed without naming directions (the e64 B value is printed '64- 1/4"' with a stray space on p. 9; the guide writes 64-1/4", which check_numbers flags). Floating Mantel Kit dimensions (Figure 3.8, p. 29), base-bracket positions (Figures 2.7-2.9), the wall-mount electrical box zone (Figure 2.17), log layouts (pp. 35-40) and the two control-panel pairing buttons (Figure 5.1, p. 41) exist only as figures and are referenced, not transcribed. No troubleshooting chart or code table; the fault panels and the owner troubleshooting drawer are built from statements on pp. 7, 41 and 43-46. Left out: the down-light '-'/'+' buttons, which p. 45 says adjust 'light brightness from number 1 to 7' although the same passage gives 5 brightness settings on the arrows and p. 42 lists seven down-light colors. p. 43 says to press an 'unlock' button after safe mode while p. 44 says to press power once to unlock; both are repeated as written. The lock feature (hold on/off 60 seconds) is as printed. The same control is called main power switch (p. 42), main switch (p. 41), rocker switch (p. 44) and toggle switch (p. 46); each term is kept in context. Catalog features not in the manual: a real-timber log set, a black surround and named flame colors; the catalog's '13 ember-bed colors' correspond to the manual's 13 floor LED colors (the ember bed is a red pulsating LED, pp. 42 and 45).
